2.4 Overall Efficiency

We have examined both the algorithmic and computational efficiency of MCMC algorithms, each of which fundamentally affect overall MCMC efficiency. We define the overall efficiency of W simply

as E(V) = A(V)/C(V). We consider this to be a sensible measure of the overall efficiency of an

MCMC algorithm, since E(V) may be interpreted as the number of effective samples produced per unit of MCMC algorithm runtime, for the slowest mixing model parameter. If we can construct W to maximize E(V), then V is the most time-efficient MCMC algorithm for generating effectively independent samples to approximate the true, joint posterior distribution of O.

That being said, from our examination of algorithmic and computational efficiency, it is not immediately clear how to balance tradeoffs between A(V) and C(V) to maximize E(V). We have

generally considered the two boundary-case algorithms scalar and Ublock, but a huge number of intermediate algorithms exist. For V € UM, we may gain useful insights regarding the factors
